metrics.name: Total security incidents
metrics.definition: Total number of confirmed security incidents recorded in the reporting period.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates overall threat pressure and reporting maturity; raw volume alone does not measure security posture.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.
Interpretation is context-dependent; a change is not automatically good or bad.

metrics.name: Material security incidents
metrics.definition: Incidents that met the organisation's materiality criteria (financial, operational or regulatory impact).
metrics.executive_meaning: The clearest Board-relevant measure of realised business impact from security events.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.
Materiality criteria differ by organisation; state the definition used.

metrics.name: Critical security incidents
metrics.definition: Incidents classified as critical under the organisation's severity methodology.
metrics.executive_meaning: Signals severity concentration and the potential for significant disruption or loss.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: High-severity security incidents
metrics.definition: Incidents classified as high severity under the organisation's severity methodology.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the volume of serious events short of the critical threshold.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Ransomware incidents
metrics.definition: Number of confirmed ransomware-related incidents in the period.
metrics.executive_meaning: Board-critical due to potential for severe operational, financial and reputational harm.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Phishing incidents
metrics.definition: Number of confirmed phishing incidents affecting users or systems.
metrics.executive_meaning: Reflects the effectiveness of email controls and human-risk mitigation.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Business email compromise incidents
metrics.definition: Number of confirmed business email compromise incidents.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates exposure to financially motivated impersonation and payment fraud.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Account compromise incidents
metrics.definition: Number of confirmed incidents where a user or service account was compromised.
metrics.executive_meaning: Signals the effectiveness of identity and access controls.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Insider-related security incidents
metrics.definition: Confirmed incidents involving malicious or negligent insider activity.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates insider-risk exposure and the effectiveness of data and access monitoring.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Third-party security incidents
metrics.definition: Security incidents originating from, or involving, third-party suppliers or partners.
metrics.executive_meaning: Highlights supply-chain and ecosystem risk exposure outside direct operational control.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Mean Time to Detect (MTTD)
metrics.definition: Average elapsed time between the start of a detectable security event and its detection.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates detection effectiveness and operational responsiveness.
caveats: Durations depend on consistent start/stop definitions across the periods being compared.

metrics.name: Mean Time to Respond (MTTR)
metrics.definition: Average elapsed time from detection to an effective response starting.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates containment responsiveness and the maturity of incident handling.
caveats: Durations depend on consistent start/stop definitions across the periods being compared.

metrics.name: Mean Time to Contain
metrics.definition: Average elapsed time to contain an incident after detection.
metrics.executive_meaning: Reflects the ability to limit blast radius once an incident is identified.
caveats: Durations depend on consistent start/stop definitions across the periods being compared.

metrics.name: Mean Time to Eradicate
metrics.definition: Average elapsed time to eradicate the threat from affected systems.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates how quickly environments are returned to a trusted state.
caveats: Durations depend on consistent start/stop definitions across the periods being compared.

metrics.name: Mean Time to Recover
metrics.definition: Average elapsed time to restore normal service after an incident.
metrics.executive_meaning: Links security response to business recovery and availability.
caveats: Durations depend on consistent start/stop definitions across the periods being compared.

metrics.name: High-severity alert volume
metrics.definition: Number of high-severity alerts generated in the period.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates detection coverage and SOC load; not directly a measure of security posture.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.
Interpretation is context-dependent; a change is not automatically good or bad.

metrics.name: Alert-to-incident conversion rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of alerts that convert into confirmed incidents.
metrics.executive_meaning: Helps assess alert quality and triage effectiveness.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.
Interpretation is context-dependent; a change is not automatically good or bad.

metrics.name: Automated response rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of qualifying alerts handled by automated response playbooks.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates operational efficiency and the balance between automation and human analysis.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Detection coverage
metrics.definition: Estimated proportion of the estate covered by active detection controls.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates visibility and the breadth of monitoring across the environment.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Incident recurrence rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of incidents that recur from a previously unresolved root cause.
metrics.executive_meaning: Signals whether root causes are genuinely remediated or merely suppressed.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Total open vulnerabilities
metrics.definition: Total number of open vulnerabilities across the estate.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the overall size of the technical exposure backlog.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Critical vulnerabilities
metrics.definition: Number of open vulnerabilities classified as critical under the chosen severity methodology.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the volume of high-severity technical exposure requiring prioritised treatment.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: High-severity vulnerabilities
metrics.definition: Number of open vulnerabilities classified as high severity.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the volume of serious, though non-critical, exposure.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV)
metrics.definition: Number of open vulnerabilities known to be actively exploited in the wild.
metrics.executive_meaning: A sharper signal of real-world exploitation risk than raw severity counts.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Internet-facing critical vulnerabilities
metrics.definition: Critical vulnerabilities present on assets directly reachable from the internet.
metrics.executive_meaning: Combines severity with external exposure, raising the likelihood of exploitation.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Vulnerability remediation SLA compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of vulnerabilities remediated within the agreed SLA.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates whether exposure is being closed at the pace the organisation has committed to.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Mean time to remediate
metrics.definition: Average elapsed time to remediate a vulnerability from detection.
metrics.executive_meaning: Reflects remediation throughput and the ability to reduce exposure over time.
caveats: Durations depend on consistent start/stop definitions across the periods being compared.

metrics.name: Critical vulnerability remediation backlog
metrics.definition: Number of critical vulnerabilities past their remediation due date.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates unresolved high-severity exposure that has breached committed timelines.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Vulnerability backlog ageing
metrics.definition: Average age of open vulnerabilities in the backlog.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates whether exposure is accumulating or being actively worked down.
caveats: Durations depend on consistent start/stop definitions across the periods being compared.

metrics.name: External attack-surface exposure score
metrics.definition: Composite score representing external attack-surface exposure.
metrics.executive_meaning: Summarises how much externally reachable, potentially exploitable surface exists.
caveats: Scores are only meaningful against their own defined scale and methodology.
Scores are methodology-dependent; compare against your own baseline only.

metrics.name: Critical patch compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of assets patched for critical vulnerabilities within policy windows.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates hygiene discipline against the highest-risk software flaws.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: High-risk patch compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of assets patched for high-risk vulnerabilities within policy windows.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates breadth of patch discipline beyond the most critical flaws.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Endpoint patch compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of endpoints meeting patch policy.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates endpoint hygiene and the effectiveness of patch management.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Server patch compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of servers meeting patch policy.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates server estate hygiene, where exploitation can be highly impactful.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Network-device patch compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of network devices meeting patch policy.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates perimeter and network-device hygiene.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Secure-configuration compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of assets meeting the agreed secure configuration baseline.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates resilience against misconfiguration-driven exposure.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: CIS benchmark compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of assets compliant with the applicable CIS benchmark.
metrics.executive_meaning: Provides a comparable configuration-hygiene signal against a recognised baseline.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.
A CIS benchmark is a configuration baseline, not a certification of security.

metrics.name: Unsupported / end-of-life asset count
metrics.definition: Number of assets running unsupported or end-of-life software.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates structural exposure that cannot be fully patched.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Configuration drift rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of assets that have drifted from the approved baseline.
metrics.executive_meaning: Signals the durability of configuration controls over time.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Unauthorised software rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of assets running unauthorised software.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates control over the software supply within the estate.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: MFA coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of relevant accounts protected by multi-factor authentication.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the breadth of a foundational control that blunts credential-based attacks.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Privileged-account MFA coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of privileged accounts protected by multi-factor authentication.
metrics.executive_meaning: Signals protection of the accounts that could cause the greatest harm if compromised.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Passwordless authentication coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of authentication enabled through passwordless methods.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates modernisation of identity assurance and reduction of credential risk.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Privileged account count
metrics.definition: Number of privileged accounts in the environment.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the size of the high-impact attack surface through privileged access.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Dormant-account count
metrics.definition: Number of active accounts with no recent legitimate use.
metrics.executive_meaning: Signals latent access that could be abused with reduced detection.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Excessive-privilege findings
metrics.definition: Number of findings where accounts hold more access than required.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates least-privilege discipline and potential blast radius.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Privileged-access review completion
metrics.definition: Proportion of scheduled privileged-access reviews completed on time.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates governance rigour over the most sensitive access.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Joiner-mover-leaver SLA compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of joiner/mover/leaver access changes completed within SLA.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates control over access lifecycle and reduction of orphaned access.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Identity-related incidents
metrics.definition: Confirmed incidents attributable to identity or access weaknesses.
metrics.executive_meaning: Reflects the real-world effectiveness of identity controls.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Privileged-access violations
metrics.definition: Number of confirmed violations of privileged-access policy.
metrics.executive_meaning: Signals governance gaps and misuse risk in high-impact access.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: EDR coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of endpoints covered by active endpoint detection and response.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the breadth of endpoint visibility and response capability.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Endpoint security-policy compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of endpoints compliant with the endpoint security policy.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates endpoint configuration discipline.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Endpoint encryption coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of endpoints with full-disk encryption enabled.
metrics.executive_meaning: Reduces data-loss impact from lost or stolen devices.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Mobile-device management coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of mobile devices under management.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates control over mobile endpoints and their data.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Network segmentation coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of the environment subject to effective network segmentation.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates containment potential and limits lateral movement.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Zero-trust control coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of the environment covered by zero-trust access controls.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates architectural maturity in limiting implicit trust.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Secure web-gateway coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of users or traffic protected by a secure web gateway.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates control over web-borne threats.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Cloud workload security coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of cloud workloads covered by security controls.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates visibility and protection across cloud environments.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Cloud configuration compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of cloud resources compliant with the secure baseline.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates resilience against cloud misconfiguration exposure.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Internet-facing asset count
metrics.definition: Number of assets directly reachable from the internet.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the size of the externally exposed attack surface.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.
Interpretation is context-dependent; a change is not automatically good or bad.

metrics.name: Sensitive-data discovery coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of the data estate scanned for sensitive-data discovery.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates whether the organisation knows where its sensitive data resides.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Sensitive-data encryption coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of sensitive data stores with encryption at rest applied.
metrics.executive_meaning: Reduces impact from data exposure and unauthorised access.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Data-loss-prevention coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of relevant channels covered by data-loss-prevention controls.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates control over data egress across key channels.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Data-loss-prevention incidents
metrics.definition: Number of data-loss-prevention incidents recorded.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the volume of policy-relevant data movement attempts.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Data-access anomalies
metrics.definition: Number of anomalous data-access events detected.
metrics.executive_meaning: Signals potential insider-risk or compromised-account behaviour.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Excessive data-access privileges
metrics.definition: Number of findings where data access exceeds business need.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates least-privilege discipline over sensitive data.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Data-breach incidents
metrics.definition: Number of confirmed data-breach incidents involving personal or sensitive data.
metrics.executive_meaning: Board-critical due to regulatory, financial and reputational consequences.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Records affected by security incidents
metrics.definition: Number of data records affected by security incidents in the period.
metrics.executive_meaning: Quantifies the scale of data impact behind incident counts.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Backup coverage for critical data
metrics.definition: Proportion of critical data covered by the backup regime.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the recoverability of the organisation's most important data.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Recovery-test success rate for critical data
metrics.definition: Proportion of critical-data recovery tests that succeeded.
metrics.executive_meaning: Provides evidence that critical data can actually be recovered, not just backed up.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Critical-service availability
metrics.definition: Availability of defined critical services over the period.
metrics.executive_meaning: Relates security and resilience directly to business operations.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Cyber-related service downtime
metrics.definition: Total downtime of services attributable to cyber events.
metrics.executive_meaning: Quantifies realised operational impact from security incidents.
caveats: Durations depend on consistent start/stop definitions across the periods being compared.

metrics.name: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of critical systems recovered within their Recovery Time Objective.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates whether recovery capability matches business expectations.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Recovery Point Objective (RPO) compliance
metrics.definition: Proportion of critical systems meeting their Recovery Point Objective.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates acceptable data-loss tolerance in recovery.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Disaster-recovery readiness
metrics.definition: Assessed readiness of disaster-recovery capability.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates preparedness before a major disruption occurs.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Disaster-recovery exercise success rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of disaster-recovery exercises that met their objectives.
metrics.executive_meaning: Provides evidence that recovery plans work in practice.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Backup success rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of scheduled backups that completed successfully.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the reliability of the recovery foundation.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Immutable backup coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of backups stored in immutable form.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates ransomware resilience of the backup estate.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Restore-test success rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of restore tests that successfully recovered data or systems.
metrics.executive_meaning: Demonstrates that recovery is proven, not merely planned.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Business-continuity exercise completion
metrics.definition: Proportion of planned business-continuity exercises completed.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates operational discipline in validating continuity arrangements.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Security-awareness completion rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of staff who completed required security-awareness training.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates training compliance; not, by itself, behavioural effectiveness.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Phishing-simulation failure rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of recipients who fail phishing simulations.
metrics.executive_meaning: A behavioural signal of human-risk exposure, distinct from training completion.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Repeat phishing-failure rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of users who repeatedly fail phishing simulations.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates concentrated, persistent human-risk exposure.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Security-training hours per employee
metrics.definition: Average security-training hours delivered per employee.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates investment in security awareness, not directly its effectiveness.
caveats: Durations depend on consistent start/stop definitions across the periods being compared.

metrics.name: Security-policy acknowledgement rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of staff who have acknowledged current security policies.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates policy adoption and basic governance coverage.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Security-reporting rate by employees
metrics.definition: Rate at which employees report suspected security events.
metrics.executive_meaning: A positive engagement signal; higher reporting can improve detection.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Human-related security incidents
metrics.definition: Confirmed incidents with a significant human-factor contributor.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates realised human-risk impact.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: High-risk user population
metrics.definition: Number of users identified as high-risk based on behaviour or role.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the size of the population most exposed to social engineering.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Security-culture survey score
metrics.definition: Composite score from security-culture surveys.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates staff attitudes and engagement with security beyond compliance.
caveats: Scores are only meaningful against their own defined scale and methodology.
Survey scores depend on instrument design and are not directly comparable across organisations.

metrics.name: Security-training exception rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of staff with unapproved exceptions to required training.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates gaps in baseline security awareness coverage.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Residual cyber-risk score
metrics.definition: Aggregate residual cyber-risk score after controls.
metrics.executive_meaning: Provides a consolidated view of risk remaining after mitigation, against the organisation's own methodology.
caveats: Scores are only meaningful against their own defined scale and methodology.
Risk scores are methodology-dependent; compare only against your own baseline and scale.

metrics.name: Inherent cyber-risk score
metrics.definition: Aggregate inherent cyber-risk score before controls.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the underlying risk profile independent of control effectiveness.
caveats: Scores are only meaningful against their own defined scale and methodology.
Risk scores are methodology-dependent; compare only against your own baseline and scale.

metrics.name: Risk-appetite breach count
metrics.definition: Number of breaches of the Board-approved risk appetite.
metrics.executive_meaning: A direct governance signal that tolerance thresholds have been exceeded.

metrics.name: Open high-risk findings
metrics.definition: Number of open findings rated high risk.

metrics.name: Overdue audit findings

metrics.name: Regulatory findings

metrics.name: Security-policy exception count

metrics.name: Risk-acceptance count

metrics.name: Control-testing pass rate

metrics.name: Security-assurance coverage
metrics.definition: Proportion of the control environment covered by independent assurance.

metrics.name: Critical suppliers assessed

metrics.name: Critical supplier assessment coverage

metrics.name: Critical supplier high-risk findings

metrics.name: Cybersecurity programme completion rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of the cybersecurity programme delivered against plan.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates execution momentum of the security strategy.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Strategic security initiative delivery rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of strategic security initiatives delivered on schedule.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates whether strategic change is keeping pace with intent.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.
Track delivery against an agreed baseline; a single late initiative may be material by itself.

metrics.name: Cybersecurity staff headcount
metrics.definition: Number of staff dedicated to cybersecurity.
metrics.executive_meaning: Context for capacity to execute the security programme.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.
Interpretation is context-dependent; a change is not automatically good or bad.

metrics.name: Cybersecurity vacancies
metrics.definition: Number of open cybersecurity positions.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates capacity risk and potential execution constraints.
caveats: Absolute counts are influenced by detection, reporting maturity and the size of the environment.

metrics.name: Cybersecurity staff turnover
metrics.definition: Annualised turnover of cybersecurity staff.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates retention risk and continuity of security capability.
caveats: Percentage figures depend on a consistent measurement universe and methodology.

metrics.name: Cybersecurity capability / maturity score
metrics.definition: Composite maturity score for cybersecurity capability against the organisation's chosen model.
metrics.executive_meaning: Indicates the overall maturity trajectory of the security programme.
caveats: Maturity scores are methodology-dependent and not directly comparable across frameworks.
Maturity scores are model-dependent and not directly comparable across frameworks or organisations.
